title: Decision Models Beat Generation on Cost

questions.prompt: A loop makes about 40 calls per task: 35 decide something, 5 write user-facing text. Which calls should run on the large generation model?
options: The 5 that write text a human reads
The 35 decisions, because decisions are harder
questions.explanation: Only the generation calls produce something anyone reads, so they justify the larger model. 'Decisions are harder' is the tempting answer, but the output-token cost is driven by how much text comes back, and a decision needs almost none.

questions.prompt: Why is output token count the cost driver for a decision call?
options: A generation model answers a yes/no with a paragraph, and you are billed for that paragraph
Decisions use a more expensive model tier
Output tokens are billed at a fixed rate per call
questions.explanation: The input is often the same chunky context either way; the waste is the sentence the model writes when a label would do. 'Input tokens are free' is false — the point is that output is where the decision version costs more than it needs to.

questions.prompt: A teammate wants every decision call to write out its reasoning, for auditability. What is the cost, and when is it worth paying?
options: No cost; text is always cheap
It turns a decision into a generation call, so you pay for the prose; worth it when the explanation is genuinely read
It is impossible with current models
questions.explanation: Asking a decision to explain itself is asking a generation call, and output tokens are the bill. The tempting answer is 'no cost', but the whole lesson is that prose you throw away is still billed — the exception is prose that a person actually audits.

questions.prompt: When is a decision model the wrong tool?
options: When the answer is one of six fixed categories
When the task is open-ended and has no defined correct answer to compare against
questions.explanation: A decision model needs a closed set of answers and a way to tell a good label from a bad one. Fixed categories, high volume, and private input are the situations where it is *right*. Without a defined correct answer, a smaller model just fails faster and cheaper.
